claim.why_it_matters: The four sub-headings of 4.3.8.2 are plain paragraphs; the parallel sub-headings of 4.3.8.3/4.3.8.4 on page 168 are marked '#####'. A heading missing or at the wrong level breaks the section structure that navigation and clause lookup by section number rely on; the wording itself is intact.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 167 (folio IV-21) prints 4.3.8.2 Subscripting and its four numbered sub-headings, 4.3.8.2.1 Function, 4.3.8.2.2 General Format, 4.3.8.2.3 Syntax Rules and 4.3.8.2.4 General Rules, as section headings. The sub-headings are bold. In page-167.md all five are plain paragraphs with no '#' marker. In page-168.md the parallel headings are marked: '#### 4.3.8.3 Function-Identifier', '##### 4.3.8.3.1 Function' through '##### 4.3.8.4.4 General Rules'. The heading wording is intact and nothing is missing. The defect is structural: anything that locates clauses by markdown heading cannot find 4.3.8.2 or its sub-clauses. The claim is accurate except that it leaves out the parent heading 4.3.8.2 Subscripting, which is also an unmarked plain paragraph.
